clue.text: Huge wastage in fuel

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside the other, the waste inside the fuel

parts.note: coal is a fuel
wastage is loss

explanation.surface: A complaint about enormous amounts of fuel going to waste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LOSS inside COAL, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of enormous size; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Accident victims have no ties-such being their wear ?

indicators.note: have no tells us that something is lost from the victims, here the ties are dropped

parts.note: the people hurt in an accident are its casualties
taken as written, the neckties

explanation.surface: People hurt in a crash, their neckties loosened, are dressed informally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have no' takes TIES off the end of CASUALTIES; informal clothes without a tie are called casual wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal clothing is described as casual, so it is the kind of wear meant.

clue.text: Diet item leads to fast time by the Italian

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: Fasting season brings an Italian's pulse dish to the table.
explanation.definitionFit: This small pulse is a staple food, an item of a diet.

clue.text: Make this pup settle down with his six brothers?

definitions.text: Make this pup settle down with his six brothers?

indicators.note: make here asks us to make a new word out of the letters that follow, rearranging them

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A request to get a puppy to lie down among its six brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make' rearranges the letters of PUP SETTLE. A puppy with six brothers is one of seven born together.
explanation.definitionFit: One of seven offspring of a single birth is called by this name.

clue.text: Showing aversion or opposition to Beethoven's sonata ?

parts.note: anti means against, in opposition to
Beethoven's Sonata Pathétique, its title given in English spelling

explanation.surface: A music lover who dislikes or is against one of Beethoven's sonatas.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Piano Sonata No. 8 is the Pathétique; the clue reads its name as the English word PATHETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling deep dislike means being hostile, which this adjective expresses.

clue.text: They're matters of form

parts.note: matters of form sounds like etiquette, but literally they are forms or outlines

explanation.definitionFit: Outlines or figures are forms, so they are literally matters of form.

clue.text: The card to beat

parts.note: sounds like the card in a game that must be beaten, but read as one of a suit of playing cards and an organ that beats

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a playing-card suit and the organ that beats in the chest.

clue.text: They make way for others

parts.note: make way sounds like stepping aside, but means opening a path for followers

explanation.definitionFit: Early settlers and explorers go first and open the way for those who follow.

clue.text: Right opposite Compton Mackenzie's street

definitions.meaning: the Latin word for left, the opposite of right
Compton Mackenzie wrote the novel ... Street

explanation.surface: Someone giving directions to a house across the road from a novelist's.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry the left side is called by the Latin for left, and Mackenzie's 1913 novel bears the same word in its title.

clue.text: After effects of getting a tanning in a string vest?

definitions.text: After effects of getting a tanning in a string vest?

parts.words: After effects of getting a tanning in a string vest?
parts.note: a tanning sounds like a beating, but sunbathing in a mesh vest leaves a pattern of small tanned dots

explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the word means sunburnt spots; usually it names dark patches on the sun.

clue.text: A moron perhaps to leave alone

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be put another way, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An idiot might be abandoned somewhere on his own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of A MORON.
explanation.definitionFit: To strand someone on a desert island, leaving them with no company, is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Post for one of the steering committee on board?

definitions.text: Post for one of the steering committee on board?

parts.words: Post for one of the steering committee on board?
parts.note: on board suggests a ship's crew steering, but the board is a company board and the post is a seat on it

explanation.definitionFit: The office held by a member of a company's board is so named.

clue.text: Tavern widow's farewell

parts.note: points to the song There Is a Tavern in the Town, whose forsaken heroine sings her goodbye in French

explanation.walkthrough: The chorus of the old song There Is a Tavern in the Town ends 'Adieu, adieu, kind friends, adieu', sung by a woman left alone by her lover.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for goodbye, used in English as a formal farewell.

clue.text: There's no object in not scoring

definitions.meaning: something with no purpose has no point
a team with no points is not scoring

explanation.surface: A coach complains there is no purpose in a match without goals.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both futile, having no purpose, and scoreless, with no points.

clue.text: The one to put your shirt on

definitions.text: The one to put your shirt on

parts.words: The one to put your shirt on
parts.note: putting your shirt on a horse means betting all you have, but here a shirt is hung on a frame

explanation.definitionFit: A wooden frame for drying laundry, on which a shirt is hung.

clue.text: Simple-minded trader ?

parts.note: simple-minded sounds like foolish, but simples are medicinal plants and this trader minds them

explanation.definitionFit: A seller of medicinal plants, which were once called simples.

clue.text: Cues held in a different form

indicators.note: in a different form tells us to put the letters into another arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Prompts are kept in another format.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a different' rearranges the letters of CUES HELD; the last word, 'form', is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A printed form or table to fill in is a list of entries, as is a timetable.

clue.text: He was all at sea when flying

definitions.text: He was all at sea when flying

parts.words: He was all at sea when flying
parts.note: points to the legendary ghost ship and its captain, doomed to sail forever, the Flying one

explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Flying sea captain was a man from the Netherlands.

clue.text: Not that you see them fooling round the Old Bailey

definitions.text: Not that you see them fooling round the Old Bailey

parts.words: Not that you see them fooling round the Old Bailey
parts.note: the Old Bailey is a law court, but the fools meant served at a royal court

explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bailey is London's central criminal court; the fools meant belong to a king's court.
explanation.definitionFit: Professional fools kept at a royal court to entertain the monarch.

clue.text: You're on a winner, my friend, in the matter of housing.

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts one piece on top of the next

parts.note: pal is a friend
an ace is a winning serve in tennis

explanation.surface: A friend assures you that a property deal is a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts PAL above ACE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand residence is a place where royalty are housed.

clue.text: On going away, they should, not be missed!

definitions.text: On going away, they should, not be missed!

parts.words: On going away, they should, not be missed!
parts.note: going away is leaving on honeymoon, and once married they are no longer called Miss

explanation.definitionFit: Women leaving on honeymoon have just married and are now Mrs rather than Miss.

clue.text: On the up and up, like Longfellow's youth

definitions.meaning: the Latin motto meaning ever higher
the youth in Longfellow's poem carries a banner bearing this word

explanation.surface: A rising young man compared to the hero of a Victorian poem.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin motto means still higher, and Longfellow's poem of 1841 takes it for its title.

clue.text: Nautical inclinations

parts.note: inclinations sounds like preferences, but means a ship leaning to one side

explanation.definitionFit: A ship that leans to one side is said to do this; the noun names those tilts.

clue.text: Robin in full song

parts.note: robin sounds like the bird singing, but it is the first word of a song's title

explanation.walkthrough: Robin Adair is a traditional Irish song; the full title adds the surname to Robin.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname that completes the old song title Robin Adair.

clue.text: But two-thirds majority is the limit

indicators.note: two-thirds of a three-letter word keeps two of its letters, here the final pair

parts.note: the majority is most

explanation.surface: A remark that a two-thirds majority is as far as one can go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two-thirds' keeps UT, the last two of the three letters of 'But'.
explanation.definitionFit: The greatest possible extent is the furthest point, the boundary.

clue.text: A thin lad astray in the East

indicators.note: astray means gone off course, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A skinny boy gets lost while travelling in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astray' rearranges A THIN LAD; the definition names a country located in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: This Southeast Asian kingdom lies in the East.

clue.text: He might resent reform

indicators.note: reform means form again, so the letters are reshaped into a new word

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who would be bitter about changes to the system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges RESENT into a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, so a 'he'.

clue.text: Clean advice to the over observant

definitions.meaning: read as ..., telling someone who notices too much to stop spotting things

explanation.surface: A tip for a fussy person who always finds a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: Without a single mark means immaculately clean; split in two it urges noticing fewer things.
